note: The Game's own sentences (noughts and crosses): B2 at its hardest. Never used by the Board, the Ultimate Challenge or Defuse.
focus: Conditionals at their hardest: inversion, mixed times, and alternatives to if.

rounds.prompt: ___ I known the road was closed, I would have taken the train.
rounds.note: Had + subject + past participle = If I had known: a third conditional without if.

rounds.prompt: If she hadn't missed that flight, she ___ in Rome now.
rounds.note: Mixed conditional: a past cause (hadn't missed) with a present result (now).

rounds.prompt: Take an umbrella ___ it rains later.
rounds.note: In case = as a precaution, before anything happens. With if you would take it only once it rains.

rounds.prompt: ___ it not been for the lifeguard, the boy would have drowned.
rounds.note: Had it not been for = If it hadn't been for: a past condition.

rounds.prompt: ___ you need any help, just give me a ring.
rounds.note: Should + subject + verb = if, for something possible but not expected.

rounds.prompt: ___ to the bank yesterday, I would have enough cash to pay you now.
rounds.note: Inverted mixed conditional: past action (had gone), present result (would have now).

rounds.prompt: You can borrow my laptop ___ you bring it back by Friday.
rounds.note: Provided that = only if this condition is met.

rounds.prompt: ___ you to win the lottery, what would you do first?
rounds.note: Were + subject + to-infinitive: a formal, very hypothetical future.

rounds.prompt: But ___ your help, I would never have finished the project.
rounds.note: But for + noun = if it hadn't been for.

rounds.context: You didn't study medicine, so you are not a doctor today.
rounds.line: If you had studied medicine, you ___ a doctor now.
rounds.note: Past cause, present result: would + infinitive.

rounds.context: There is a small chance of snow. Then the match will be cancelled.
rounds.line: ___ it snow, the match will be cancelled.
rounds.note: Should it snow = if it happens to snow.

rounds.context: She isn't coming, but you will still have fun.
rounds.line: You'll enjoy the party ___ she doesn't come.
rounds.note: Even if = whether or not this happens, the result is the same.

rounds.context: The only way you will get in is with a ticket.
rounds.line: You won't get in ___ you have a ticket.
rounds.note: Unless = except if.

rounds.context: He regrets shouting at his boss yesterday.
rounds.line: If only he ___ at his boss yesterday!
rounds.note: If only + past perfect: a regret about the past.

rounds.prompt: If I ___ (not/oversleep) this morning, I wouldn't be in such trouble now.
rounds.note: Mixed: the past perfect for the past cause, would for the present result.

rounds.prompt: ___ (you/need) anything else, please don't hesitate to contact us.
rounds.note: Should you need = if you need: formal, polite, typical of letters.

rounds.prompt: Were the government ___ (raise) taxes again, there would be protests.
rounds.note: Were + subject + to + infinitive.

rounds.prompt: Had the warning ___ (give) earlier, fewer people would have been injured.
rounds.note: Inverted third conditional in the passive: had + subject + been + past participle.

rounds.prompt: If it weren't for his injury, he ___ (play) in last night's final.
rounds.note: Present state (his injury), past result (last night): would have + past participle.

rounds.prompt: Had it not been ___ the rain, we would have finished the match.
rounds.note: Had it not been for = if it hadn't been for.

rounds.prompt: I'll lend you the money on condition ___ you pay me back by June.
rounds.note: On condition that = only if.

rounds.prompt: You'd better leave now, ___ you'll miss the last bus.
rounds.note: Otherwise / or = if you don't.

rounds.prompt: ___ I to tell you the truth, would you promise not to be angry?
rounds.note: Were I to tell you = if I told you.

rounds.prompt: Build the sentence.
rounds.note: Inverted third conditional.

rounds.prompt: Build the sentence.
rounds.note: Were it not for = if it weren't for (present).

rounds.prompt: Build the sentence.
rounds.note: Should + subject + verb for a possible future.

rounds.prompt: Build the sentence.
rounds.note: Mixed: past cause, present continuous result.

rounds.prompt: Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: Had I known, I would have come.
Were she here now, she'd know exactly what to say.
Should you see him, tell him to call me.
Did I know the answer, I would tell you.
rounds.answer: Did I know the answer, I would tell you.
rounds.note: Only had, were and should invert in conditionals: If I knew the answer, I would tell you.

rounds.prompt: Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: If I were you, I wouldn't trust him.
If he had left earlier, he would be here by now.
Unless you don't book now, the tickets will sell out.
Provided you pay in advance, you'll get a discount.
rounds.answer: Unless you don't book now, the tickets will sell out.
rounds.note: Unless already means if not: Unless you book now, the tickets will sell out.

rounds.prompt: Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: I wish I had listened to you.
If only I knew her number!
I wish you would stop interrupting me.
I wish I would be taller.
rounds.answer: I wish I would be taller.
rounds.note: Wish + would is for other people's annoying habits, not your own states: I wish I were taller.

rounds.prompt: Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: But for the rain, we would have won.
Supposing you lost your job, what would you do?
If it will rain, the match will be cancelled.
As long as you're careful, you can borrow my car.
rounds.answer: If it will rain, the match will be cancelled.
rounds.note: No will after if for a future condition: If it rains, …

rounds.prompt: Mixed or third?
items: If I'd taken the job, I'd be rich now.
If she hadn't left, she'd still be here.
Had he trained harder, he'd be in the team today.
If I'd taken the job, I'd have moved to Paris.
Had we known, we'd have stayed at home.
If you'd called, I'd have picked you up.
rounds.note: A mixed conditional ends in the present (now, still, today).

rounds.prompt: If not, or only if?
rounds.note: Unless, otherwise and or else carry the not; provided that, as long as and on condition that set a condition.

rounds.prompt: Correct or wrong?
items: Should it rain, we'll stay in.
Had they not helped, we'd have failed.
Hadn't they helped, we'd have failed.
If I'd known, I'd tell you yesterday.
Would you come, I'd be happy.
rounds.note: Inversion keeps not after the subject (Had they not), and would never starts an if-clause.

rounds.prompt: Match each inversion to its if-clause.
rounds.note: Had, were and should can replace if.

rounds.prompt: Match each word to its meaning.
rounds.note: Four ways to set a condition without if.

rounds.prompt: Match the halves.
pairs: I could afford that car now.
I wouldn't have shouted at my sister.
Had the train been on time,
we wouldn't have missed the wedding.
rounds.note: Mixed, mixed, third and first: each half needs its partner's time.

rounds.prompt: We only arrived on time because you lent us your car.
rounds.stem: ___ your car, we wouldn't have arrived on time.
rounds.note: Had it not been for / But for = if it hadn't been for (which is six words — too many).

rounds.prompt: I didn't know you were ill, so I didn't visit you.
rounds.stem: ___ you were ill, I would have visited you.
rounds.note: Had I known = if I had known.

rounds.prompt: If you need any help, just call me.
rounds.note: Should you need = if you need.

rounds.prompt: I regret not taking that job in Berlin.
rounds.note: Wish + past perfect for a past regret.

rounds.prompt: You can go to the party, but you must be home by midnight.
rounds.stem: You can go to the party ___ home by midnight.
rounds.note: As long as = on condition that.

rounds.prompt: He didn't take his medicine, which is why he's still ill.
rounds.stem: If he had taken his medicine, he ___ ill.
rounds.note: Mixed: past cause, present result.

rounds.prompt: If they don't reduce the price, I won't buy it.
rounds.stem: I won't buy it ___ the price.
rounds.note: Unless = if … not.

rounds.prompt: Without the map, we would have got lost.
rounds.stem: If it ___ the map, we would have got lost.
rounds.note: If it hadn't been for = without.

rounds.sentence: Unless you don't apologise, she won't speak to you again.
rounds.note: Unless already contains the not.

rounds.sentence: If I would have known about the strike, I would have taken a taxi.
rounds.note: No would in the if-clause: if I had known.

rounds.sentence: Had I not been so tired, I would go to the concert last night.
rounds.note: Last night is past: would have gone.

rounds.sentence: If I were you, I will apologise to her straight away.
rounds.note: Advice with If I were you takes would.

rounds.sentence: Should you will need more information, please contact our office.
rounds.note: Should + bare infinitive: Should you need.

rounds.sentence: I wish I can speak Japanese as fluently as you.
rounds.note: Wish + past (could) for a present wish.

rounds.sentence: Take your coat in case it will get cold later.
rounds.note: No will after in case: in case it gets cold.
